newsitem.title: UK: Yeltsin recovery sends Russian debt prices higher.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin recovery sends Russian debt prices higher.

text.p: Russian debt prices opened stronger on Wednesday, boosted by news that President Boris Yeltsin is recovering from heart surgery.

Brokers said Vneshekonombank paper -- some $32 billion of old Soviet debt which is close to being restructured -- opened about one point higher at 79 to 80 cents in the dollar, nearing record highs touched early last month.
Yeltsin met his Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Wednesday and promised to be back soon at his Kremlin desk.
The Kremlin press service said Yeltsin had come off a lung ventilator this morning, a sign he was recovering well.
"It's one major concern out of the way. Things are looking positive," one trader said.

Vnesh dollar debt, which surged 150 percent in value this year, hit a record of 82 cents in early October, but subsequently retreated sharply on profit-taking, prompted by jitters over the country's stability.
